answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Each submission hangs on the saffron of a task receipt, and the harbor is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, slashed on a failed audit. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the karst of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
